speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me evaluate the newborn's feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting, could you please tell me the infant's age in days and whether they have passed any meconium stools yet?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The infant is only six hours old, which makes pyloric stenosis highly unlikely given the typical onset at 2-6 weeks. I need to know if the newborn has passed any meconium stools since birth, as failure to pass meconium within the first 48 hours is a key indicator for conditions like Hirschsprung disease or meconium ileus.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the newborn passed any meconium stools since birth, and does the physical exam reveal any abdominal distension or visible peristaltic waves?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Brother had pyloric stenosis. Social history: NA

speaker: Doctor
text: I still need to know if the infant has passed meconium and what the abdominal examination shows, such as distension or a scaphoid abdomen. Please clarify these physical findings.

speaker: Patient
text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur heard at the left mid to lower sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The dysmorphic features strongly suggest Down syndrome, which is highly associated with duodenal atresia presenting with bilious vomiting. I will request an abdominal X-ray to look for the classic double bubble sign. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray
